name: ALFAUR
question: Does alfuzosin before catheter removal improve trial without catheter success after a first BPH-related acute urinary retention episode?

design.population: 363 men older than 50 years with a first episode of spontaneous acute urinary retention attributed to benign prostatic hyperplasia and 500–1500 mL drained at emergency catheterization were randomized; 360 received first-phase treatment.
design.description: Double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial at 71 centers in Europe and South Africa with second-phase rerandomization
design.locator: Full text (2005 report), Methods, p 84; Table I, p 85

verdictNote: The initial voiding-trial endpoint improved; six-month surgery incidence did not differ significantly.
takeaway: After emergency catheterization for first BPH-related acute urinary retention, alfuzosin 10 mg once daily before catheter removal improved successful voiding versus placebo (146/236 [61.9%] versus 58/121 [47.9%]; P = 0.012); six-month surgery incidence after rerandomization did not differ significantly.

reports.label: Initial voiding-trial report
reports.dateLocator: Crossref and PubMed give June 2004 without a day
reports.citation: McNeill SA, Hargreave TB; Members of the Alfaur Study Group. "Alfuzosin once daily facilitates return to voiding in patients in acute urinary retention." *J Urol.* 2004;171(6 Pt 1):2316-2320. doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000127743.80759.7a
reports.followUp: Catheter removed after at least two doses of blinded treatment; satisfactory voiding without recatheterization assessed within 24 hours; one additional tablet given the following day.

results.measure: Satisfactory voiding within 24 hours after catheter removal without recatheterization; no postvoid-residual threshold specified; risk difference in percentage points
results.note: Risk difference calculated from reported rounded percentages; TWOC data were available for 357 patients (236/121).
results.locator: Full text, Methods and Results, p 2317

results.endpoint: Adjusted odds of successful trial without catheter
results.measure: Alfuzosin versus placebo after adjustment for age and drained volume
results.note: Across arms, successful voiding was 49.0% at age 65 years or older versus 74.1% below 65, and 47.8% with drained volume 1,000 mL or greater versus 66.7% below 1,000 mL (both P less than 0.001). Backward logistic regression found lower odds with age 65 years or older (OR 0.309, 95% CI 0.182–0.514) and drained volume 1,000 mL or greater (OR 0.361, 95% CI 0.225–0.571); both P less than 0.0001. These prognostic analyses were not designated secondary endpoints.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 2317; Table 3, p 2318

harms.label: At least one adverse event during the initial phase
Orthostatic hypotension during the initial phase
harms.note: Two alfuzosin recipients withdrew because of postural hypotension.

harms.label: Adverse-event withdrawals during the initial phase
harms.note: Alfuzosin: two postural hypotension, one catheter-related infection, one unrelated hemorrhoids; placebo: one catheter-related infection.

delivery.label: Initial treatment and voiding trial
delivery.value: Emergency urethral catheterization, then alfuzosin 10 mg once daily or placebo in a 2:1 allocation; catheter removed after at least two doses, with one additional tablet the next day. Mean catheterization was 53 ± 10 hours with alfuzosin and 52 ± 12 hours with placebo; voiding was assessed within 24 hours of removal.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods and Table 1, p 2317

reports.label: Six-month surgery phase
reports.dateLocator: Crossref and PubMed give January 2005 without a day
reports.citation: McNeill SA, Hargreave TB, Roehrborn CG; Alfaur Study Group. "Alfuzosin 10 mg once daily in the management of acute urinary retention: results of a double-blind placebo-controlled study." *Urology.* 2005;65(1):83-89. doi:10.1016/j.urology.2004.07.042
reports.followUp: Six months after blinded rerandomization of successful voiding-trial participants; 169 were rerandomized and 165 received treatment.
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Results, p 85; Table I, p 85

results.endpoint: BPH surgery after successful trial without catheter
results.measure: Six-month BPH surgery; Kaplan–Meier surgery-free survival difference in percentage points
results.note: Of 204 successful TWOCs, 169 were rerandomized (85/84) and 165 received treatment (82/83); the effect is the reported surgery-free survival difference, not the raw surgery-risk difference.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 85; Table I, p 85

results.endpoint: BPH surgery at one month after successful trial without catheter
results.measure: One-month BPH surgery; Kaplan–Meier surgery-free survival difference in percentage points
results.note: Event counts come from 5/14 and 13/20 of the respective six-month surgery totals; percentages use the 82/83 treatment-exposed denominators.
results.locator: Full text, Abstract, p 83; Results, p 85

results.endpoint: BPH surgery at three months after successful trial without catheter
results.measure: Three-month BPH surgery; Kaplan–Meier surgery-free survival difference in percentage points
results.note: Event counts come from 8/14 and 17/20 of the respective six-month surgery totals; percentages use the 82/83 treatment-exposed denominators.
results.locator: Full text, Abstract, p 83; Results, p 85

results.endpoint: Lower urinary tract symptoms and bother at treatment end
results.measure: Last-assessed IPSS and IPSS bother score
results.note: IPSS P = 0.012; bother-score P = 0.004. The paper does not designate these as secondary endpoints or give a prespecified success threshold, arm-specific numbers assessed, or confidence intervals.

harms.label: Serious adverse events and adverse-event withdrawals during second phase
harms.note: Serious-event percentages are published without event counts or explicit event denominators; 82/83 received second-phase treatment.

harms.label: Potentially vasodilatory adverse events during second phase
harms.note: Dizziness, postural hypotension or hypotension, malaise, and syncope were grouped; none occurred in the second phase.

delivery.label: Second-phase treatment
delivery.value: Of 204 men with successful trial without catheter, 169 were blindly rerandomized (85 alfuzosin, 84 placebo); 165 received six months of assigned alfuzosin 10 mg once daily (82) or placebo (83). BPH surgery was assessed at one, three, and six months. Scheduled surgery criteria included peak flow below 5 mL/s, postvoid residual above 350 mL, IPSS above 25, recurrent urinary tract infection, progressive uropathy, macroscopic hematuria, and patient request.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, p 84; Results and Table I, p 85
